events.title: Okta Threat Intelligence: AI attack frameworks favor mail.tm disposable email to sign up Auth0 and Okta accounts in identity attacks; ARTEX is one of the frameworks named
events.summary: Okta Threat Intelligence published the threat advisory on Nov 24, with Permiso. Attackers bulk-register accounts with disposable email on Auth0 tenants and Okta organizations that allow public self-service registration. The activity began in June 2026 and accelerated at scale in October and November. In P0 Labs (Permiso) data, eighty percent of attacker hosts where disposable email was found used mail.tm. Okta says the agents chose the service at run time, across four autonomous penetration-testing frameworks including ARTEX. The mailbox domain returned by mail.tm was maxxspace.com on Sep 13 and fldubai.com from Oct 30.

attributes.mail.tm share: About 80% of attacker hosts where disposable email was found
attributes.Timing: Began in June, accelerated at scale in October and November

events.title: ARTEX first public release (v0.1.0)
events.summary: Autumn-27/ARTEX made its first commit and released v0.1.0. v0.3.14 was released on Sep 24, and v0.3.15 was tagged on Oct 7.

attributes.License: AGPL-3.0. Censys says this applied from Jul 26; piyolog says it was adopted only on Sep 18
attributes.Public release year: Goumang writes 2025, treated as a typo

events.title: Microsoft: ARTEX searches GitHub for leaked secrets, 5 minutes to Key Vault exfiltration
events.summary: Heavy querying of GitHub for secrets since August 2026. From Oct 28, leaked application credentials were used to sign in to Entra ID as service principals. In at least one case, it took only 5 minutes from searching GitHub to Azure Key Vault exfiltration. Todyl reports a similar campaign from the same IPs: from Nov 1, stolen Entra application credentials were used to sign in to MSP environments, reaching 27 organizations.

attributes.Window: Searches since August; sign-ins since Oct 28 (Microsoft); since Nov 1 (Todyl)
attributes.Todyl scale: About 45 app registrations at roughly 18 organizations targeted; more than 33 authenticated; 27 organizations reached
attributes.Todyl access: 81 files; about 2,279 mailbox items; searches across about 25 tenants
attributes.Todyl speed: 95% scripted-client sign-ins; up to 24 sign-ins in 10 seconds

events.title: Profero: a Hong Kong operator chains ARTEX with a private AI attack suite behind a 273,000-node residential proxy pool to attack web applications
events.summary: Profero published a report on Oct 31: an operator in Hong Kong is chaining ARTEX with a private suite of AI attack agents (the Ultra suite) behind a residential proxy pool of about 273,000 nodes to attack internet-facing web applications, and has already hit multiple Profero customers. In the suite, a vulnerability workbench finds and proves flaws and ARTEX drives exploitation. Profero saw the exploitation stage against targets; scanning preceded exploitation by days, and data left in base64 chunks of about 1,800 bytes. Profero found no sector focus and advises treating the targeting as opportunistic.

attributes.Proxy pool: Residential proxy pool of about 273,000 nodes
attributes.Timeline: Related infrastructure first seen Aug 2; an active engagement in late October

events.title: Operator prompts mention organizations in 19 countries and regions
events.summary: In operator records recovered by Zscaler, prompts asked for scans of organizations in these places. No attacks were confirmed and no victims were reported.

attributes.Countries and regions: 19 (listed in the blog, number not written); CRN says 19; Daily CyberSecurity banner says 20

events.title: Mandiant incident response: multiple actors use ARTEX
events.summary: Observed since late August. Includes profit-driven actors conducting data-theft extortion. Webshells were dropped by writing to logs, and results were sent back through 491 rotating webhook.site URLs.

attributes.Speed: One operation: 27 events in 23 seconds; individual commands compressed to about 2 to 25 seconds
attributes.Scale: One operation enumerated more than 110,000 AD objects and 1,300+ internal users

events.title: Small Indian NBFCs lose about ₹300 crore (media estimate)
events.summary: ₹300 crore is 3 billion rupees. It is a media estimate, not a total confirmed by the RBI.

attributes.Losses: About ₹300 crore over two months (Economic Times-affiliated reports); The 420 says 18 months
attributes.Cases: About 150 complaints or FIRs; another analysis gives 255 cases and about ₹72 crore; the two do not match

events.title: Seoul police: about 90 organizations, about 8.2 million records (separate case)
events.summary: Police call it South Korea's first large-scale hacking case using generative AI. About 90 organizations and about 8.2 million records.

attributes.Time: Aug 31 to Oct 13, "60 organizations in 44 days" (Decrypt); AI attacks on 60 organizations (SBS)

events.title: GMO: about 20 Japanese companies targeted from ARTEX infrastructure
events.summary: GMO confirmed ARTEX on the attack-source infrastructure, which targeted about 20 Japanese companies. GMO assesses that targets were selected by country and industry. The intelligence was handed to law enforcement.

attributes.Targets: About 20 companies (GMO blog); about 80 (Yomiuri and NHK-affiliated reports, not in the GMO blog, basis unexplained)
attributes.Time window: Sep 18 to Oct 18 appears only in Yomiuri-affiliated reports, not in the GMO blog
attributes.Attack infrastructure: 1 server with confirmed ARTEX; another 6 servers

events.title: UK: 123 Reg customer data accessed
events.summary: Involves contact details, customer relationship data, company VAT numbers and API product information. The number of affected customers was not disclosed.

attributes.Disclosure date: The Register Oct 28; Seoul Economic Daily says Oct 30
attributes.Data scope: Customer email says read-only; spokesperson says it may have been copied

events.title: GoDaddy Websites + Marketing data access on the same day
events.summary: According to a notice posted by a customer, a third party read W+M profile and settings data through an API on the same day. GoDaddy has not confirmed a link to the 123 Reg incident.

events.title: DIVD in the Netherlands breached
events.summary: Breached through two Zammad zero-days (CVE-2026-102489, 102490). Exfiltration of volunteer user data is confirmed, and several systems show signs of partial exfiltration. No signs were seen for HR, source code, Slack or finance.

attributes.Speed: Initial access to root: seconds (Update #4, BleepingComputer); 12 minutes (Update #8)
attributes.Detection: Detected in 19 minutes; versus intrusion on Sep 21 and detection on Sep 22

events.title: Unit 42: ARTEX abused exposed APIs and probed identity providers to break into customer cloud environments
events.summary: Unit 42 Incident Response investigated multiple intrusions involving ARTEX, and Managed Threat Hunting tracked a coordinated campaign against customer cloud environments in sectors including retail and consulting. The attacks used no software vulnerability, turning public password reset pages and exposed APIs into cloud access, sometimes in less than a day. An Oct 30 indicator note says the activity ran from Sep 24 to Oct 27 and is ongoing.

attributes.Timeline: Sep 24 to Oct 27 (indicator note; described as ongoing)
attributes.Scale: Multiple intrusions; no victim count given
attributes.Speed: More than 200 client secrets validated in about three minutes; pivots within about a minute of a credential download
attributes.Exposure: 609 internet-facing hosts running ARTEX as of October

events.title: First wave of intrusions at Korean financial institutions (7 institutions)
events.summary: The earliest known attack date is Sep 27. The first report to the authorities came on Sep 30 (Shinhan). Disclosures followed from Oct 1 to Oct 4. The attack surface was mainly external-facing edge applications, and the methods included SQL injection and authentication bypass. A Financial Security Institute (FSI) official said it was not a fully autonomous attack without human involvement.

attributes.Shinhan: 25,729 (Herald Business, National Assembly audit materials); 25,727 (CEO Score and others)
attributes.Attack IPs: FSS: 19 IPs, 12 countries (Financial News, Oct 6); 28 IPs, 12 countries (industry sources); 33, or 28 after deduplication (Genians); more than 20 IPs across more than 10 countries (WSJ, as relayed); CrowdStrike lists 9 proxy IPs
attributes.Reason for the block (Woori): Five accounts: intrusion prevention system; no such vulnerability; multi-factor authentication; luck; Xint inspection (sources include the vendor)
attributes.Attack IPs (MONITORAPP): About 50 attacker IPs and C2 domains (Nov 8)

events.title: Korean financial intrusions expand to 16 institutions
events.summary: Beyond the first wave of 7, another 9 were confirmed, for a total of 16 institutions and about 100,000 records. The list includes P2P firms, crypto-asset firms and Saemaul Geumgo (MG Community Credit Cooperatives). Information that allows direct fraudulent use, such as account numbers and card numbers, was not confirmed. SBS reported in the same period that data leaked at some institutions included account numbers. The two accounts differ.

attributes.DB Savings Bank: Company says it blocked the attack; FSC lists it among the 16; News1 estimates 142 people

events.title: ARTEX user targets IT and software vendors (Wiz / UNC7228)
events.summary: Password spraying against Okta and Entra and attacks on internal login pages, with some sessions lasting 24 to 30 hours. Wiz says most attempts failed. GTIG reports intrusions and data theft.

attributes.Start: Wiz blog: October; GTIG relay: at least August

events.title: S-RM incident response: multiple intrusions used ARTEX
events.summary: S-RM says it responded to severe intrusions at several organizations in October. It groups motives into three categories: supply chain (one attempt against an MSP), payment card theft, and unknown but with potential for mass disruption. S-RM says the intrusions were identified and contained before the agents could complete their intended impact.

attributes.Speed: One case: all identity infrastructure, cloud systems, source code and perimeter firewalls compromised in 24 hours. Another: from a web server to central management platforms in 4 hours
attributes.Persistence: Pivoted within 10 minutes and began using TOR exit nodes. In one case the agents regained access to the environment on three separate occasions

events.title: Microsoft: Storm-3358 uses ARTEX against Southeast Asian financial institutions
events.summary: It scanned internet-facing systems, exploited flaws such as anonymous file upload and SSRF, then used netcat and curl to download open-source remote access tools such as WISP, vshell and AdaptixC2 for persistence and lateral movement. Microsoft gave no count of victim organizations or countries and published 8 IP indicators.

attributes.Window: Started in October (Microsoft); indicators first seen Oct 19 to Nov 2, still active as of Nov 6
attributes.IoCs: 8 IPs: 3 WISP C2, 4 ARTEX servers, 1 C2
attributes.Counts: Microsoft gave no count of victim organizations or countries

events.title: Datadog: ARTEX hunted for financial data and secrets in several AWS environments
events.summary: Datadog says it observed ARTEX in several real AWS environments in October, with a focus on accessing financial data. Every session opened with unauthenticated S3 read requests. One cluster entered with compromised long-term IAM keys and searched CloudWatch logs for financial institution names and secrets. Another abused public Cognito user pools to sign up, then tried read-only discovery, which failed for lack of permissions.

attributes.Timeline: Oct 20: the same compromised key used again from 103.54.154.40. Oct 26 to 27: spike in Cognito SignUp calls
attributes.Scale: "Several AWS environments"; no exact count given
attributes.Exposure: In early November, related IPs were traced to a hosted console, and hundreds of internet-exposed ARTEX consoles were found

events.title: Korean, English and Japanese localizations and derivatives appear
events.summary: The ScopeWeaver repository was created on Oct 2. The artex-ko repository was created on Oct 3 and later renamed artex-global. The earliest Japanese version dates from Oct 9. AhnLab recorded derivatives including ScopeWeaver, Tangora PTaaS, Horda, Meze, AegisLoop and Bob Research Labs.

attributes.Korean version date: Repository created Oct 3; SBS Oct 7; CSA relay Oct 8
attributes.Number of derivatives: AhnLab side says at least 50 clones and derivatives (fnnews, Oct 21)
attributes.ARTEX-Full: A derivative introduced in a WeChat post on Nov 6, connecting Nuclei, Subfinder, ScopeSentry and MCP tools
attributes.AntiFox: GitGuardian (Nov 11) calls it a fork of ARTEX; Arctic Wolf (Nov 10) reports it used in IIS and AWS intrusions

events.title: Taiwan: 91APP order database accessed
events.summary: The attacker entered through the internal tool Appsmith, obtained a database key from GitLab and accessed an order database. No credit card or other payment information was involved. The stolen data was later used in scam messages targeting brand customers.

attributes.Scope: 1,329 brands, 4,798,255 consumers (91APP's determination by maximum possible scope; an upper limit, not a confirmed leak count)
attributes.Early figures: Dozens of brands; the last six months or so, or two months
attributes.Incident date: Material information filing says Oct 14; letter to brands says Oct 3

events.title: Amazon: decoy sensors captured ARTEX agents' campaign records, covering AI credential theft and deepfake identity checks
events.summary: Amazon's MadPot decoy sensor network received requests from AI agents that carried the agents' own campaign records. The records show two campaigns: large-scale theft of API keys and cloud credentials that grant access to AI models, and deepfake attempts to defeat identity verification at two cryptocurrency exchanges, which the verification vendor rejected every time. Amazon cannot verify the outcomes the agents reported and has notified potentially affected customers.

attributes.Scale: Hundreds of targets, mainly AI application platforms
attributes.Deepfake: 11.5 frames per second on a single consumer GPU; rejected every time
attributes.Concurrency: At least four agent sessions ran at once
attributes.Indicators: 11 IPv4 addresses with first and last seen dates

events.title: Public detection rules and internet-mapping queries
events.summary: artex-ko added Sigma rules on Oct 5. Theori created aipt-detections on Oct 12 and published a white paper on Oct 15. Censys, Hunt.io and RST Cloud published internet-mapping queries, and BadByte published YARA rules. Cisco Talos published Snort rules and an IoC file on Nov 13. Google SecOps said on Nov 17 that it has deployed rulepacks to detect ARTEX.

events.title: Public ARTEX console counts
events.summary: Methods and dates differ by vendor. AhnLab cautions that these IPs cannot all be treated as attacker addresses. Censys says about 650 are hosts with the same configuration, and about 815 deployments are actually distinguishable.

attributes.Censys distribution: United States 726, Hong Kong 387, China 177, Japan 51, Singapore 38, South Korea 21 (Nov 3)
attributes.Censys overlap: 155 hosts (10.6%) carry another threat detection; 32 open directories (Nov 5)
attributes.GitGuardian: 1,428 Shodan services matched the ARTEX family (Nov 7; counted as services, not hosts)
attributes.FBI: More than 1,600 (early November, citing Censys; Censys's own post says 1,465)
attributes.Cisco Talos: More than 2,500 ARTEX-associated C2 IPs (no date); IoC file lists 2,546, of which 1,480 are also in the ThreatBook Feed (this site's comparison)

events.title: Upstream repository taken down, project goes closed-source
events.summary: Wayback recorded the first upstream 404 at Oct 8 10:15 UTC. The statement on the author's profile page is dated Oct 8. The statement says public updates have stopped. The official image autumn27/artex has been removed from Docker Hub.

attributes.Date: Statement Oct 8; byteiota says Oct 9; Check Point says both Sep 8 and Oct 8 in the same article; Genians says removed before Oct 11

events.title: Forks and copies surge after takedown
events.summary: Backups and English versions began appearing within two minutes of the upstream takedown. GitHub search on Nov 6 shows existing repositories with artex in the name: 15,529 forks since Sep 27, 15,826 including non-forks, and 10,493 from Oct 8 to Oct 14.

attributes.Wiz: more than 12,000 forks (Oct 22), dated to Oct 8, which does not match the archives: there were only a few hundred forks before the takedown
attributes.piyolog: Oct 20: the main 15 lineages total more than 12,000, not deduplicated
attributes.Cloudflare: Over 12,000 repositories; 204 public repositories with their own code changes; ARTEX and its forks are over 60% of known AI penetration testing orchestrators (Nov 12)
attributes.ReversingLabs: 11 fork families share one Go engine; 184 operator binary samples across Linux, Windows and macOS (Nov 18)

events.title: Poisoning: popular copy swapped to a backdoored Docker image
events.summary: trhhubsd/ARTEX changed only one line of docker-compose.yml, swapping the image to tomicdd/artex. The image hides unauthenticated command execution in the login endpoint. It exists only in the precompiled binary, so it cannot be seen by reading the source. A second image, congdonglinux/artex, has the same digest. Docker removed both images on Nov 5.

attributes.Account: tomicdd registered Oct 8 18:50 UTC, pushed 19:41 UTC
attributes.Exposure: 62 consoles (58 IPs, 4 domains, Nov 2 to Nov 4), 46 still the backdoored version. This is exposure, not confirmed compromise. BadByte says 62 is a lower bound
attributes.Residual: 637 GitHub repositories still point to the image; imxv/ARTEXX took over 630 forks

events.title: India CERT-In: CRAFTY FALCON attacks the financial sector
events.summary: Severity is Critical. This is an update to CIAD-2026-0046 of Oct 9. The attacker called the victims' own payment and lending APIs, ran small tests of 1 rupee and then moved to large amounts. The public version has no victims, counts or IoCs. Full IoCs are given only to BFSI entities in the TLP version.

events.title: Brandefense: a single operator used ARTEX for reconnaissance and vulnerability probing against 76 payments and Web3 organizations (Operation LedgerSwarm)
events.summary: Odin by Brandefense published the report on Nov 19. Brandefense analyzed the operator's exposed campaign archive: 39 ARTEX task records with metadata, consuming about 10.8 billion input tokens. Seven early tasks are dated Oct 9 to 12, and 23 more ran from Nov 4 to 9. The operator ran reconnaissance against 76 organizations in 18 sectors, enumerating 13,864 subdomains, 1,105 of them live. ARTEX produced 6,124 "findings", 941 critical and 2,173 high, but these are model-assigned labels and were not verified. On Nov 9 and 10 the operator switched to task templates that lock workers to whitelisted domains and block neighbouring-address scans. Brandefense's two-week observation window ends on Nov 18.

attributes.Targets: 76 organizations in 18 sectors: payments and fintech 21, Web3/DeFi/stablecoin 20, enterprise tech 11, iGaming 10, banking and insurance 8, crypto exchanges 6
attributes.Findings: 6,124, of which 941 critical and 2,173 high; all unverified model labels
attributes.Tasks: 39, about 10.8 billion input tokens; early tasks Oct 9 to 12, 23 more from Nov 4 to 9

events.title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup credentials abused; Storm-0940 targets M365 tenants
events.summary: Discovered on Oct 14, disclosed on Oct 16, attributed by Microsoft on Oct 21. Most targets were not successfully compromised, but several attacks gained privileged cloud access, some in under 3 hours from first targeting to privileged access. Microsoft gave no count of successes.

events.title: Check Point: misconfigured ARTEX instances expose cybercrime operations
events.summary: Most attacks run fully autonomously once the target is set. Configurations mainly use Chinese models, with DeepSeek Flash the most common.

events.title: VAPOR PANDA uses ARTEX to target more than 200 organizations
events.summary: A single ARTEX controller was directed at at least 14 countries within 11 days. 200+ is the number of targets, not compromises. ARTEX was not the only tool: the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor, webshells, Chisel and SoftEther were also used.

attributes.Possible: About 140, about 70% confirmed or possibly compromised at medium confidence (CyberScoop citing CrowdStrike)

events.title: Follow-on intrusions in Korea's financial sector (cumulative 37 institutions, 40 incidents)
events.summary: The Financial Services Commission (FSC) said on Nov 5 that from Sep 30 to Nov 3 there were intrusion reports from 37 institutions covering 40 incidents and about 473,000 records, and that some small institutions had about KRW 1 billion of self-managed funds stolen. The list was not published. 22 institutions have been publicly named. Many were entered through groupware or external connection points. The FSC ordered about 580 financial firms to run a full check, and the FSS plans to call in crypto-asset sector CISOs on Nov 19. As of Nov 6 there is no public report of a final penalty or an arrest in the financial cases. On Nov 9 the Financial Security Institute (FSI) found that its information-security regular assessment support system had been accessed abnormally from outside and some information had leaked. It reported this to the FSC and suspended the system. The reports do not mention ARTEX.

attributes.Institutions: 37 institutions, 40 incidents (FSC, Nov 5, as of Nov 3)
attributes.Leaked: About 473,000 records (a count of records, not people)
attributes.Stolen funds: About KRW 1 billion (FSC); Pravang about KRW 100 million, Zoomfund KRW 300 million (media)
attributes.Bithumb: Several hundred records; about 800; 7,155; 7,159 (different times and sources)
attributes.GOPAX: 7 users and 2 current or former staff (from early September); further leak in October; all deposits, withdrawals and trading halted after an extortion email on Nov 6
attributes.Follow-up: Full check of about 580 firms: external access points of registered systems by Nov 30, all by Dec 31; FSS meeting of crypto-asset CISOs on Nov 19
attributes.FSI: About 200 administrative forms, more than 300 personal records in those forms and more than 350 system-user records (Yonhap, Nov 10); data of 30 to 40 financial companies leaked (Seoul Shinmun summary box, not in the article body)

events.title: Japan: Onamae Desktop Cloud breached
events.summary: The attacker demanded about JPY 8 billion. GMO says no link to ARTEX has been established.

attributes.Ransomware: AP-affiliated reports say deployed; BleepingComputer says not activated; TechNode says no traces found

events.title: Microsoft: Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet use ARTEX
events.summary: No target organizations are described. Microsoft assesses that these actors mainly use AI to enhance existing techniques.

events.title: European Commission internal HR systems hit with an AI tool, services down for more than 10 days, EU Academy user names and emails exposed; CERT-EU says similar activity highly likely used ARTEX
events.summary: The European Commission detected an intrusion on Oct 22, confirmed it as a cyberattack on Oct 26 and took several applications offline as a precaution. The Sysper HR platform and the medical reimbursement system were affected, leaving staff unable to handle timesheets, leave and reimbursements for a period; translation services were also hit. The Commission confirmed the incident publicly on Nov 19, saying most applications were restored, no evidence of a data breach affecting all staff had been found, no ransom was demanded, and the European Data Protection Supervisor had been notified. On Nov 23 the Commission disabled public access to its EU Academy learning platform, confirmed it was hit by the same attack and that user names and email addresses were exposed, and warned users to be wary of unexpected emails.

attributes.Disruption: Internal HR, payroll, medical reimbursement and translation services down for more than 10 days
attributes.Timeline: Detected Oct 22, confirmed Oct 26, made public Nov 19
attributes.EU Academy: Public access disabled on Nov 23; user names and email addresses exposed; number affected not disclosed

events.title: JPCERT/CC alert Case E: attack attempts abusing AI penetration testing platforms
events.summary: The alert confirms attack attempts, not victims. The listed IPs may also have legitimate uses.

attributes.Publication date: at260030 published Oct 8, updated Oct 9 and Oct 23

events.title: WorkOS internal tool accessed by a researcher's ARTEX agent
events.summary: The first confirmed unauthorized access to the internal tool's API was on Oct 25, and records were retrieved in bulk on Oct 30. Only sales and customer support data was involved, including contact details, account relationships, and summaries of sales and support calls and Slack. There is no evidence that application data was accessed. WorkOS says the researcher contacted it from Nov 3 to 5 with evidence, and deleted all the data without sharing it. The number of affected customers and records was not disclosed.

attributes.Timeline: Oct 25 first unauthorized API access; Oct 30 bulk retrieval; Nov 3 to 5 researcher made contact
attributes.Characterization: Nov 2 bulletin: unauthorized access by an AI-assisted offensive security framework; Nov 6 update: a researcher's agent escaped unintentionally, not malicious
attributes.Root cause: The internal tool's API was reachable from the internet; it accepted a weak credential meant for local development; it had no rate limits; the first access on Oct 25 went unnoticed until Oct 30
attributes.Remediation: From Nov 3, WorkOS regularly tests its internet-facing systems with ARTEX, looking for unnecessary exposure and guessable credentials

events.title: Bitrise publishes ARTEX intrusion report: a dormant test bot account without 2FA led to a chain of cloud keys within ten hours and a platform-wide shutdown
events.summary: Bitrise published an incident report on Nov 19. From Oct 25, ARTEX scanned its public surface while labelling itself an authorized pentest; on Nov 12 it returned as an ordinary customer and tested cross-tenant access without success. On Nov 13 the attacker signed in to a dormant internal test bot account without two-factor authentication and was using cloud keys within 11 minutes, then chained into signing files, source code, infrastructure state and build logs. Bitrise shut the whole platform down that day, revoked all 919 cloud service-account keys, rotated every production secret and rebuilt its build infrastructure. When the attacker replayed stolen credentials on Nov 18, every read was refused.

attributes.Speed: First cloud key in use 10 min 37 s after the dormant account sign-in; last successful call 10 h 11 min after sign-in
attributes.Customer impact: Files in 15 customer workspaces accessed: 1 signing certificate file (its password was not obtained), 1 provisioning profile, 13 build logs
attributes.Response: 919 cloud service-account keys revoked, all production secrets rotated, build servers in three data centers rebuilt

events.title: Chainstack breached
events.summary: Entered the development environment through a third-party component on Oct 26, entered part of the production environment on Oct 29, and was discovered and cut off on Oct 31. May include organization names, account holder names, member emails and password hashes. Node credentials are treated as exposed.

events.title: Chainalysis discloses intrusion
events.summary: The first notice on Oct 30 said there was no evidence of access to investigation content, authentication credentials or session tokens. The Nov 4 update said that on Nov 2 the company found names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all users exposed. KYT, Address Screening and the login page went offline, and all users must reset passwords and rotate API keys. Reactor, KYT and Address Screening were back online on Nov 7. The entry point and duration were not disclosed.

attributes.Scope: Oct 30: no evidence of access to investigation content, credentials or session tokens; Nov 4: names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all users exposed
attributes.Services: Nov 4: KYT, Address Screening and the login page offline; Nov 7: Reactor, KYT and Address Screening back online

events.title: Barracuda: attacker used a cloud key leaked from an AI vendor to enter its cloud environment; activity matches ARTEX
events.summary: A cloud access key that Barracuda gave an AI company and did not revoke after the project ended was exposed when that company's development environment was compromised. On Nov 1 and 2 the attacker used it to touch about 10 cloud accounts in roughly 44 hours, moved into a data analytics system, a source code token and Kubernetes clusters, harvested credentials widely and hunted for cryptocurrency wallet material. The attacker could reach a system that stores XDR customer integration credentials, but there is no direct evidence those credentials were viewed. Barracuda asked affected XDR customers to recreate their integration credentials.

attributes.Timeline: Nov 1 04:33 to Nov 2 23:31 (UTC), about 44 hours; discovered Nov 4
attributes.Scope: About 10 cloud accounts across five platforms
attributes.Entry: Unrevoked cloud access key given to a third-party AI company
attributes.Customer impact: No direct evidence that customer integration credentials were viewed; notified Managed XDR Cloud and Monitored Endpoint customers must recreate credentials
attributes.Indicators: 4 IP addresses (3 IPv4, 1 IPv6), 5 user agents

events.title: Dragos canary study: at least three AI providers leaked user prompts, and the attacker abusing canary AWS keys added ARTEX in November
events.summary: Dragos Chief Research Officer HD Moore published the findings on Nov 19. From July to November 2026, the team sent about two million prompts to AI services, each carrying a unique trackable canary credential, and watched where those credentials were used. Data from at least three AI providers was exposed; none of the three knew until Dragos told them, and the earliest incident dates back to mid-July. The largest breach involved a couple hundred canary AWS keys: the attacker first tested whether each key was live, in some cases within hours of the prompt; then listed S3 buckets and searched Secrets Manager and Parameter Store; and tried enabling Bedrock models, creating Bedrock API keys and adding its own IAM users to keep access. From Nov 1, the same attacker added ARTEX.

attributes.Study period: July to November 2026, about two million prompts carrying canary credentials
attributes.Scale: The largest breach involved a couple hundred canary AWS keys; the canary keys were used for tens of thousands of AWS API calls in total
attributes.ARTEX: Appeared from Nov 1 and made only a handful of calls to confirm existing keys were still live

events.title: Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs: more than 10 companies reported attacks, mostly AI-related
events.summary: At a Nov 11 press conference the Ministry of Digital Affairs said more than 10 companies had reported being hit, five or six of them large. The Administration for Cyber Security said attackers mostly exploited known high-risk flaws in PHP, Node.js and GitLab and high-privilege APIs to pull large amounts of personal data, and that preliminary investigation links most cases to AI attacks, including automated attacks combined with ARTEX.

attributes.Reports: More than 10 companies, five or six of them large (Nov 11)
attributes.Timeline: Attack dates not reported; the date shown is the press conference date
attributes.Methods: Known high-risk flaws in PHP, Node.js and GitLab; high-privilege APIs with bulk data access

events.title: Salesforce: multiple actors used ARTEX to try to get into customer Salesforce environments
events.summary: Salesforce Threat Intelligence says it observed a stolen-credential-driven campaign that reached Salesforce customer environments through compromised application credentials and trusted integration sessions. The actors used environments as relays to connected services, deployed code tailored to each environment, tested account permissions and kept trying other paths after failures. Salesforce says the activity did not result from a platform vulnerability and that it notified affected customers directly.

attributes.Timeline: Activity dates not given; the date shown is the disclosure date
attributes.Scale: No count of affected customers given

events.title: Eye Security: ARTEX intrusion at a European e-commerce platform used Git-backed deployment for persistence
events.summary: Eye Security described a multi-day intrusion through a custom PHP upload flaw. Stolen credentials enabled pivots into cloud secrets and Git, where deployment changes created malicious Kubernetes workloads. Automation rebuilt deleted workloads, and the attacker returned less than an hour after service restoration.

attributes.Requests: More than 9,000 requests to one route in one minute
attributes.Adaptation: About three minutes to rewrite scripts to bypass rate limiting
attributes.Persistence: Automation rebuilt deleted malicious workloads within one second

events.title: FBI issues ARTEX advisory (FLASH-20261113-001)
events.summary: The FBI says that since at least August 2026 a variety of malicious actors have used ARTEX against many sectors worldwide, with some intrusions reaching privileged access in under three hours from initial targeting. The FLASH summarizes observed techniques, 24 IP addresses and one domain, and gives mitigations. The indicators come from earlier vendor reports and are all already listed on this site.

attributes.Speed: Some intrusions reached privileged access in under three hours from initial targeting (citing Microsoft)
attributes.South Korean finance: Personal information on about 67,000 individuals stolen (citing CrowdStrike, Zscaler, CERT-EU)
attributes.ConnectWise: Access to more than 2,250 downstream tenants (citing Microsoft)
attributes.Exposure: More than 1,600 publicly exposed consoles in early November (citing Censys)

events.title: Cloudflare: ARTEX used leaked CI/CD tokens to get into customers' Cloudflare environments
events.summary: Over the last eight weeks Cloudflare's Cloudforce One worked multiple incident response cases involving ARTEX and its derivatives. Actors first got into customers' hyperscaler environments, then used non-expiring tokens from CI/CD pipelines to move into the customers' Cloudflare environments. In one case ARTEX created many Worker scripts with artex- prefixes, sent high-rate requests including database dump requests, and attempted persistence.

attributes.Timeline: The post says only the last eight weeks; the date shown is the disclosure date
attributes.Speed: More than 69 requests per minute; 400 database dump requests in an hour
attributes.Naming: Worker script prefixes artex-, artex-pgrecon-, artex-pgw-, artex-do-

events.title: Korean university rERP systems reportedly targeted; ARTEX link and 28-university leak claim unconfirmed
events.summary: Boannews reported on Nov 17 that Team D4rkn3ttz found possible ARTEX traces and repeated targeting of university rERP research administration systems in attacker-published archives. The claimed 28 universities are not a confirmed victim count, and the researchers did not confirm a compromise of the rERP supplier.

attributes.Scope: 31 archives with 28 university names (media citing researcher analysis)
attributes.rERP: Researchers reported rERP data or collection traces in 17 university directories

events.title: Wiz: the ARTEX-Harvester campaign cluster is linked to more than a dozen organizations, reaching cloud environments through stolen version-control credentials and CI identity trust
events.summary: Wiz Research published the post on Nov 23. ARTEX-Harvester is one of about a dozen campaigns Wiz is tracking, clustered on three signals: a distinctive boto3 build, an Intent ID that increments across victims, and overlapping proxy pools. Between late October and mid-November the cluster was linked, at varying confidence, to more than a dozen organizations. The operator switched residential or ISP proxy exits on almost every request, so more than 220 IPs showed up against a single target. In one successful intrusion, the operator used stolen version-control credentials to read private repositories, then created branches that abused CI workload identity trust to reach the cloud environment, dumped CI-accessible secrets and Terraform state, and exfiltrated them. A second path started from a service-account token stolen from an application pod and ended with Kubernetes cluster-admin. Wiz also says vendors disclosed 20 more related incidents in the three weeks since its previous round-up.

attributes.Linked organizations: More than a dozen, at varying confidence, late October to mid-November
attributes.Proxies: More than 220 IPs against a single target
attributes.New disclosures: 20 more related incidents disclosed by vendors in three weeks
attributes.Exposed consoles: Wiz cites Censys counting more than 1,400 exposed ARTEX consoles in early November

events.title: NVISO: during an incident response in Belgium, ARTEX was seen deploying a new backdoor, ZQAgent, for long-term control of Linux servers
events.summary: NVISO published the post on Nov 23. During an incident response in Belgium, NVISO observed ARTEX deploying a new backdoor, ZQAgent, giving its operator a long-lasting foothold in the target environment. ZQAgent supports arbitrary code execution, file operations and network tunnelling. It migrates into an anonymous memory file and restarts as a detached process posing as dbus-daemon; its configuration is encrypted and its traffic has several encryption layers. Persistence comes in two forms: as root it writes a systemd service and an /etc/cron.d job; as another user it writes a user-level systemd service, enables lingering and adds an @reboot crontab entry. All known samples are configured with the same IP and domain as C2.

attributes.Samples: NVISO lists 3 ZQAgent samples, 2 of them public samples reported from Taiwan
attributes.C2: All known samples use the same IP and domain

events.title: JFrog: an ARTEX agent published 13 malicious model repositories on Hugging Face and, testing them on itself, leaked its operator's OpenAI key and task list to a public repository
events.summary: JFrog published the post on Nov 24. Early on Nov 24 (UTC), a newly created Hugging Face account published models carrying malicious loading code within a few hours; the payload fired once 14 seconds after upload. The payload exfiltrates the host container's environment variables to the attacker's own repositories through the Hugging Face commit API. Because the agent tested the model in its own container, the data sent to the public repository included its own ARTEX configuration, OpenAI key, database connection string and task list; the task list included phishing, SSRF probing and proxy rotation. The account was then renamed and published further models. JFrog reported it to Hugging Face the same day, and all 13 repositories were disabled by 13:29 UTC.

attributes.Timing: Account created 02:43 UTC on Nov 24, first model 03:05, all disabled by 13:29
attributes.Victims: Both collection repositories were empty when disabled

events.title: New York Times: an open-source intelligence analysis system used by the CIA, NGA and ODNI was breached; people familiar with the matter say the attackers are believed to have used ARTEX
events.summary: The New York Times reported on Nov 24, citing U.S. officials and other people familiar with the matter, that the CIA and at least two other intelligence agencies recently discovered a breach that exposed some unclassified information. The affected system is an open-source intelligence analysis system that looks for intelligence insights in public, unclassified material. It is not clear what information was compromised; classified material was not jeopardized. According to two of the people, the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence were also affected, and one said the issue had been resolved. Some of the people said the intrusion is believed to have been carried out by hackers using ARTEX. Investigators do not know who is responsible; two of the people said initial signs, including the use of ARTEX, suggest China may be behind it.

attributes.Data: Some unclassified information exposed; classified material not affected
